candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — nursing management, legal/ethical practice, communication, delegation and supervision
candidate.educational_objective: Address unsafe or unfamiliar staffing assignments before acceptance by raising competency concerns and seeking a safe resolution.

options.A: Raise the safety and competency concerns immediately with the charge nurse, clarify the assignment and available resources, and seek a safe resolution before accepting it.
options.B: Accept the assignment without discussion and rely on asking coworkers for help later, because refusing or modifying an assignment is never professionally appropriate.
options.C: Choose independently which clients to accept and leave the remaining clients unassigned, because an RN may redesign the staffing plan without notifying supervision.
options.D: Leave the facility before receiving report and send a message afterward explaining the concern, because avoiding contact with the assignment prevents abandonment or responsibility.

candidate.rationale: ANA staffing guidance directs nurses to assess patient acuity, the requirements of the assignment, available resources, and whether they have the expertise to provide the required care before accepting an assignment. Safety concerns should be raised through appropriate channels so a safe plan can be developed; unilateral abandonment or silent acceptance are not appropriate alternatives.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Before taking responsibility for an assignment requiring unfamiliar high-risk therapies, the RN should raise competence and safety concerns and seek a safe resolution rather than assuming responsibilities the nurse cannot safely perform.
candidate.source_locator: Decision-Making Framework — clarify the activity/role and determine whether it is permitted and can be performed safely under the nurse's licensure, education and competence within applicable rules and organizational safeguards
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
candidate.stem: Before accepting a new assignment, an RN learns that several assigned clients are unstable and require therapies the RN has not been trained to manage. Which action is most appropriate?
